title: I like, I love, I hate
goal: Say what you like, love and hate with aimer, adorer and détester, followed by le/la/les + a noun or by a verb, and ask other people what they like.

items.en: aimer, adorer, détester + definite article or + infinitive

drills.explain: Likes always take the definite article: cinéma is masculine → le cinéma.
musique is feminine → la musique. English says just “music”, French says “the music”.

drills.prompt: How do you say “I love travelling”?
drills.explain: After aimer, adorer and détester, the second verb stays in the infinitive, with nothing in between.
nous → aimons (or on → aime), and la before musique.

items.note: With things, aimer means “to like”. With a person, aimer alone means “to love”.

items.en: to quite like; to like (a person, as a friend)
items.note: Softer than aimer with things. With people, it means “to like” (as a friend).

items.en: to really like, to like a lot
What do you like? (to a friend)
I love it! (a thing or an activity)

example.en: I love going to the movies.
I like reading in the evening.

items.note: For now, use it only in the infinitive, after aimer, adorer or détester.

blocks.title: A conversation group at the library in Gatineau
blocks.context: Sofia and Nguyen practise French at a weekly conversation group.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Alors, Nguyen, qu'est-ce que tu aimes faire le week-end ?
lines.en: So, Nguyen, what do you like doing on weekends?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: J'adore le cinéma ! J'aime beaucoup les films français.
lines.en: I love going to the movies! I really like French films.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Moi aussi, j'aime bien le cinéma. Et tu aimes lire ?
lines.en: Me too, I quite like the movies. And do you like reading?

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Oui, j'aime lire le soir. Mais je déteste cuisiner !
lines.en: Yes, I like reading in the evening. But I hate cooking!

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Ah bon ? Moi, j'adore ça ! J'aime beaucoup la cuisine mexicaine.
lines.en: Really? I love it! I really like Mexican food.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Et la musique ? Qu'est-ce que tu aimes ?
lines.en: And music? What do you like?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: J'aime le jazz et la musique québécoise. Mais je déteste le rap !
lines.en: I like jazz and Québec music. But I hate rap!

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Ha ha ! Moi, j'adore le rap.

blocks.body: Listen first. Notice two things: after [[aime]], [[adore]] and [[déteste]] you hear either **le / la / les + a noun** ([[le cinéma]]) or **a verb ending in -er or -re** ([[lire]], [[cuisiner]]).

blocks.title: From love to hate
blocks.body:
[[Aimer]], [[adorer]] and [[détester]] are regular **-er verbs**, so you already know their endings. Here is the scale, from strongest to weakest:

- [[J'adore]]: I love (things and activities)
- [[J'aime beaucoup]]: I really like
- [[J'aime]] / [[J'aime bien]]: I like
- [[Je déteste]]: I hate

You met [[je n'aime pas]] (I don't like) in the food unit; the next lesson covers negation in full.

blocks.title: Aimer, adorer, détester in the present
head: aimer
adorer
détester
blocks.note: [[Aimer]] and [[adorer]] start with a vowel, so **je → j'** ([[j'aime]], [[j'adore]]), and you hear a *z* liaison after nous, vous, ils, elles: [[nous‿aimons]], [[elles‿adorent]].

blocks.title: Pattern 1: aimer + le / la / l' / les + noun
blocks.pattern: aimer / adorer / détester + le, la, l', les + nom
blocks.note: English often uses no article (“I like music”). French uses the definite article for likes and dislikes, because you are talking about the thing **in general**.

examples.en: Raj loves going to the movies.

examples.fr: Nous aimons beaucoup les films québécois.

blocks.title: Pattern 2: aimer + infinitive
blocks.note: To talk about an **activity**, put the second verb in the infinitive (the dictionary form), right after the first verb. Only the first verb is conjugated.

examples.en: What do you like doing? (to a friend)

blocks.body: [[La cuisine]] means **the kitchen** (you saw it in the home unit) and also **cooking / a style of food**: [[la cuisine mexicaine]] = Mexican food.

blocks.title: Why le café and not du café?
blocks.body:
In the food unit you learned [[du]], [[de la]], [[des]] for **some**: [[Je mange du chocolat]] (I'm eating some chocolate).

Likes are different: you don't like *some* chocolate, you like chocolate **in general**, as a category. French uses [[le]], [[la]], [[les]] for that general meaning.

- [[Je prends du café.]] I'm having (some) coffee.
- [[J'aime le café.]] I like coffee (in general).

examples.fr: Je mange des pommes. J'adore les pommes !
examples.en: I'm eating apples. I love apples!

blocks.title: Careful with people: aimer vs aimer bien
blocks.body:
With **things**, [[aimer bien]] is just a softer “like”. With **people**, the difference is big:

- [[J'aime Karim.]] I love Karim (romantic love).
- [[J'aime bien Karim.]] / [[J'aime beaucoup Karim.]] I like Karim (he's nice, a friend).

You will also hear [[Je t'aime]] (I love you) and [[Je t'aime bien]] (I like you). Strange but true: adding [[bien]] (“well”) makes [[aimer]] *weaker* for people. So when you talk about a colleague or a neighbour, say [[J'aime bien…]].

- **No article:** [[J'aime cinéma]] is wrong. Say [[J'aime le cinéma]].
- **Partitive instead of definite:** [[J'aime du café]] is wrong. Say [[J'aime le café]].
- **A preposition before the infinitive:** [[J'aime de lire]] is wrong. Say [[J'aime lire]].
- **Two conjugated verbs:** [[J'aime je lis]] or [[J'aime lis]] is wrong. Only the first verb changes: [[J'aime lire]].
- **“I love coffee”:** to make it clearly strong, say [[J'adore le café]]. [[J'aime le café]] usually just means “I like coffee”.

blocks.title: Magasiner and j'aime ça
blocks.body:
In Québec, “to go shopping” is [[magasiner]]: [[J'aime magasiner le samedi.]] In France, people say [[faire du shopping]] or [[faire les magasins]].

You will also hear [[J'aime ça]] (I like it) all the time, often with the thing added at the end: [[J'aime ça, le hockey !]] (I like hockey!). It is very natural spoken French.

examples.en: I love going shopping with my sister. (Québec)

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Say each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.tip: [[J'aime]] is one syllable: “jem”. The final -e is silent.

lines.en: I love going to the movies.

lines.tip: In [[déteste]] you hear the s: dé-tèst.

blocks.prompt: How does the speaker feel about rap?
blocks.explain: [[Je déteste]] = I hate. You hear the s in dé-tèst.
[[cuisiner]] = to cook. [[Lire]] is to read and [[voyager]] is to travel.

blocks.prompt: Raj talks about Olivier, a colleague he gets on well with. Which sentence means “I like Olivier”?
blocks.explain: With people, aimer bien (or aimer beaucoup) = to like. Aimer alone = to love.
optionFeedback: Without bien, this sounds like romantic love!
No article before a person's name.

blocks.text: Amira ___ marocaine et elle ___ la cuisine indienne.
blocks.en: Amira is Moroccan and she loves Indian food.
blocks.explain: Nationality uses être (elle est). “Loves” a thing = adore.
[[aiment]]: the -ent ending is silent, but you hear the z liaison: il-z‿aiment.

blocks.prompt: At the conversation group, tell a new friend two things you like, one thing you love and one thing you hate. Then ask what they like.
checklist: J'adore + a noun or a verb
Je déteste + a noun or a verb
A question: Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu aimes ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Moi, j'aime bien le cinéma et j'aime beaucoup lire. J'adore voyager ! Mais je déteste cuisiner. Et toi, qu'est-ce que tu aimes ?
models.en: I quite like the movies and I really like reading. I love travelling! But I hate cooking. And you, what do you like?

blocks.prompt: Write a short message for the conversation group's chat: three things you like or love, one thing you hate, and a question for the group.
checklist: Use le / la / les before nouns
Use at least one infinitive (lire, voyager, cuisiner…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle Lucie. J'adore la musique et j'aime beaucoup le jazz. J'aime aussi lire et voyager. Mais je déteste le sport à la télé ! Et vous, qu'est-ce que vous aimez ?
models.en: Hello! My name is Lucie. I love music and I really like jazz. I also like reading and travelling. But I hate sport on TV! And you, what do you like?

summary:
- Say what you like, love and hate: [[j'aime, j'aime bien, j'aime beaucoup, j'adore, je déteste]]
- Use **le / la / les** after these verbs ([[J'aime la musique]]) or an **infinitive** ([[J'adore voyager]])
- Know that [[J'aime bien Karim]] means “I like Karim”, but [[J'aime Karim]] means “I love Karim”
- Ask [[Qu'est-ce que tu aimes (faire) ?]]
